onboarding3d.hint: Click any step to inspect how it works in detail

steps.title: Create Account
steps.summary: Initialize administrator identity with multi-factor SSO/MFA security authentication.
howItWorks: Authenticate via Google Workspace SSO, GitHub, or Enterprise SAML 2.0.
Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA / WebAuthn FIDO2) to protect sessions.
Provision initial encryption keypairs and assign Least Privilege IAM roles.
steps.benefit: Strictly protects administrator identity against infrastructure takeover attacks.

steps.title: Create Organization
steps.summary: Set up an isolated Tenant, organize SRE/DevOps teams, and configure resource quotas.
howItWorks: Provision a logically and data-isolated Workspace (Multi-tenant Architecture).
Invite engineering team members and assign granular RBAC roles (Admin, SRE, Operator, Viewer).
Configure Resource Quotas and connect Slack, Teams, or PagerDuty alerting channels.
steps.benefit: Enforces clear permission boundaries across teams to avoid misconfigurations.

steps.title: Create Environment
steps.summary: Logically separate Production, Staging, and Dev with independent self-healing policies.
howItWorks: Create dedicated environment scopes to separate application lifecycles.
Assign Self-Healing SLA/SLO Profiles tailored to workload criticality.
Enforce strict guardrails for Production (dual confirmation for auto-scaling or rollback).
steps.benefit: Keeps Production at peak availability while Dev/Staging remain agile for testing.

steps.title: Register K8s Cluster
steps.summary: Connect securely to the Kubernetes API Server (EKS, GKE, AKS, or On-Premise bare-metal).
howItWorks: Establish an encrypted mTLS channel to your Kubernetes Cluster API Server endpoint.
Automatically inspect cluster version (v1.24 - v1.32+) and verify required CRDs.
Provision a Scoped ClusterRole ServiceAccount for telemetry reading and healing dispatch.
steps.benefit: 100% compatible with modern Kubernetes distributions without modifying host kernels.

steps.title: Generate Agent Token
steps.summary: Generate a one-time digitally signed Token to authenticate the Agent with the Control Plane.
howItWorks: Control Plane generates an Ephemeral Keypair and digitally signed JWT Token.
The token is tightly scoped to the target Cluster ID and Environment ID.
Grants telemetry push and healing-command permissions only, blocking spoofing attempts.
steps.benefit: Prevents telemetry spoofing and eliminates cluster credential leakage risks.

steps.title: Install Agent
steps.summary: Deploy the lightweight SelfHeal Agent via Helm Chart / DaemonSet with eBPF probes.
howItWorks: Run `helm install selfheal-agent` or apply the DaemonSet manifest in one command.
Agent hooks into Kubelet, Container Runtime (CRI), and kernel-level eBPF tracepoints.
Streams CPU, Memory, I/O, network drops, and pod events with microsecond overhead.
steps.benefit: Ultra-lightweight execution with zero pod restarts or cluster disruption.

steps.title: Start Monitoring
steps.summary: Activate the AI MAPE-K loop to detect anomalies and heal pods/nodes automatically.
howItWorks: Monitor: Continuously streams logs, metrics, and traces from all Pods and Nodes every 10s.
Analyze: AI Engine correlates failures (CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled, Eviction, Disk Pressure).
Plan & Execute: Runs approved remediation playbooks (restart, scale out, reroute) in <2s.
Knowledge: Persists Root-Cause Analysis (RCA) insights to prevent recurring outages.
steps.benefit: Cuts MTTR by 90%, eliminates overnight SRE toil, and sustains 99.99% uptime.
